# /backlog-autopilot-parallel (Antigravity adapter)

Canonical command: [`.claude/commands/backlog-autopilot-parallel.md`](../../../.claude/commands/backlog-autopilot-parallel.md),
which drives [`.claude/backlog-playbook.md`](../../../.claude/backlog-playbook.md).
Both are shared with Claude Code and managed by create-project, so **do not edit
them for Antigravity**.

## How to run this command here

1. Read the [`claude-compat`](../claude-compat/SKILL.md) skill first.
2. Read `.claude/commands/backlog-autopilot-parallel.md`. Wherever it says `$ARGUMENTS`, use whatever
   the user wrote after `/backlog-autopilot-parallel` (empty if nothing). Accepted arguments:
   `[--local]`.
3. Follow `.claude/backlog-playbook.md` with the parameters the command sets.
4. Each "dispatch a `task-executor` / `spec-verifier` / `task-planner` sub-agent"
   step invokes the matching custom subagent (`.agents/agents/<role>.md`) with
   `invoke_subagent` in the App and CLI. In the IDE, use the matching workspace
   skill inline instead. The safety hooks (no-commit-on-main, protect-checkout,
   and others) run through `.agents/hooks.json` in the CLI and App; still follow
   those rules yourself, since the IDE may not run them.
5. **Parallel dispatch** needs one isolated sub-agent per task, each in its own worktree (`scripts/start-task.sh` prints `WORKTREE <path>` under concurrency; the sub-agent must work only there). Without `invoke_subagent` (IDE), tell the user and offer to run the same backlog **sequentially inline** instead. Never run several tasks in one working tree.
